    Pumpkin Pie Spice Cookies

    Published: Oct 4, 2026 by Anna 3 Comments · This post may contain affiliate links ·

    Jump to Recipe Print Recipe
    Listen to audio version of this article

    Instaread

    These pumpkin pie spice cookies have slightly crisp edges and soft, chewy centers. They're flavored with brown sugar and lots of pumpkin pie spice, giving them all the warm spice flavor of pumpkin pie without the pumpkin.

    I started with my Amish sugar cookie recipe and gave it a fall twist. They're delicious with a cup of coffee or milk for a simple fall treat.

    If you prefer soft, cakey pumpkin cookies, you may want to try my iced pumpkin cookies or pumpkin whoopie pies.

    Why You'll Love These Pumpkin Pie Spice Cookies

    • Soft and chewy: These have slightly crisp edges and soft, chewy centers, more like a sugar cookie.
    • Lots of pumpkin spice: Pumpkin pie spice gives these cookies a warm, spiced flavor.
    • No pumpkin needed: You get the flavor of pumpkin pie without adding pumpkin purée.
    • No chilling: Mix, roll, and bake. There's no need to chill the dough.

    Ingredient Notes

    • Butter and oil: Using both gives these cookies buttery flavor while helping keep them soft and chewy.
    • Brown sugar: Adds a deeper flavor and helps give the cookies their soft texture.
    • Eggs: 2 large eggs plus 1 egg yolk. The extra yolk adds moisture and helps keep the cookies soft and tender.
    • Pumpkin pie spice: I use a full tablespoon for a noticeable pumpkin spice flavor without adding pumpkin.
    • Cinnamon: A little extra cinnamon complements the pumpkin pie spice and adds more warmth.
    • Cream of tartar: Helps give these sugar-cookie-style cookies their slightly crisp edges and chewy centers.
    • Rolling sugar: The sugar, pumpkin pie spice, and cinnamon coating adds a sweet, spiced finish to the cookies.

    Tips for Making Pumpkin Spice Sugar Cookies

    • Soften the butter: If you forget to set it out to soften, microwave it for about 10 seconds, then let it sit for a few minutes. You want it softened, not melted.
    • Don't overmix: After you add the flour mixture, mix the dough just until the ingredients are combined.
    • Leave room to spread: Place the dough balls a couple of inches apart on the baking sheet.
    • Watch the baking time: Smaller cookies bake faster than larger ones. Don't overbake if you want soft, chewy centers. A little extra baking time will make them more crisp.

    Storage and Freezing

    Store these cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for several days. I like to keep some out to eat over the next few days and freeze the rest as soon as they have cooled. Place the cooled cookies in an airtight container and freeze them to keep them fresh for later.

    Can I freeze the cookie dough?
    Yes. Scoop the dough into balls and freeze them on a baking sheet until firm. Transfer the frozen dough balls to a freezer bag or airtight container. When you're ready to bake, roll the frozen dough balls in the spiced sugar and bake them straight from the freezer, adding a little extra baking time as needed.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Do pumpkin pie spice cookies contain pumpkin?

    No. These cookies don't contain pumpkin puree. The warm fall flavor comes from pumpkin pie spice, cinnamon, and brown sugar.

    Is there anything I can substitute for pumpkin pie spice?

    Yes. You can make your own pumpkin pie spice with mostly cinnamon and ginger, along with smaller amounts of nutmeg, allspice, and cloves. These are the spices commonly found in pumpkin pie spice blends.

    Can I make these cookies ahead of time?

    Yes. You can bake them ahead and freeze the cooled cookies to enjoy later. Frozen cookies, stored in airtight containers, stay fresh for a couple of months.

    My Love for Fall Baking

    I love baking anytime of the year, but fall is definitely one of my favorite seasons for baking. I love all the recipes that come with the season, the warm spices and comforting fall flavors. There's nothing better than a chilly morning with a cup of coffee and a homemade pumpkin spice cookie, a pumpkin cream cheese muffin, or a slice of pumpkin coffee cake.

    These cookies are one of my favorite simple fall treats because they come together quickly without the extra step of making frosting or streusel. When I want something sweet and spiced but don't want to spend a lot of time in the kitchen, this is the kind of cookie I love to make.

    Pumpkin Pie Spice Cookie Recipe

    These pumpkin pie spice cookies have slightly crisp edges and soft, chewy centers. Made with brown sugar, pumpkin pie spice, and cinnamon, they have all the warm spice flavor of pumpkin pie without pumpkin puree.
    5 from 2 votes
    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    Prep Time 10 minutes mins
    Cook Time 10 minutes mins
    baking in batches 30 minutes mins
    Total Time 50 minutes mins
    Course Cookies, Dessert, Snack
    Cuisine American, Amish
    Servings 28 cookies
    Calories 256 kcal
    Prevent your screen from going dark

    Ingredients
      

    • 1 cup butter, softened
    • ¾ cup vegetable or canola oil
    • 1 cup brown sugar
    • 1 cup white sugar
    • 2 large eggs + 1 egg yolk
    • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
    • 4 ½ cups all-purpose flour
    • 1 teaspoon baking soda
    • 1 teaspoon cream of tartar
    • 1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice
    • ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon
    • ½ teaspoon salt
    • For rolling: ½ cup granulated sugar,1 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice,1 teaspoon cinnamon
    Get Recipe Ingredients

    Instructions
     

    • Preheat the oven to 350℉.
    • Beat the butter, oil, and sugars until well-creamed.
      1 cup butter, softened, ¾ cup vegetable or canola oil, 1 cup brown sugar, 1 cup white sugar
    • Add the eggs and vanilla, and mix well.
      2 large eggs + 1 egg yolk, 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
    • In a separate bowl, mix the flour, soda, cream of tartar, spices, and salt. Add this mixture to the wet mixture and mix only to combine.
      4 ½ cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon cream of tartar, 1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice, ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon, ½ teaspoon salt
    • In a small bowl, mix the sugar and spices for rolling the balls.
      For rolling: ½ cup granulated sugar,1 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice,1 teaspoon cinnamon
    • Scoop the dough into balls and roll each one in the sugar, spice mixture. Place them on greased or parchment-lined cookie sheets, leaving space for them to spread.
    • Bake at 350°F for 9-12 minutes, depending on the size of your cookies. The edges should be lightly golden, while the centers may still look slightly soft. Avoid overbaking if you want soft, chewy centers.
    • Let the cookies rest on the tray for a moment, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool.
    • Store cookies at room temperature for a few days. Freeze in an airtight container for longer storage.

    Notes

    • For soft, chewy cookies, don't overbake. The centers should still look slightly soft when you remove them from the oven.
    • Cookie size affects baking time. Smaller 1-tablespoon cookies take about 9-10 minutes, while larger 3-tablespoon cookies take about 12 minutes.
    • The dough does not need to be chilled before baking.
    • Yields about 28 large cookies.
    • Nutrition is approximate.
